claims.text: The FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are initially fully solid and compositionally uniform.
Chemical heterogeneity in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles promotes surface segregation at elevated temperatures.
Surface segregation creates localized defect zones at the nanoparticle surface.
Surface segregation creates surface compositional gradients.
Segregation-induced surface heterogeneity lowers the barrier for melting initiation relative to a homogeneous single-metal nanoparticle.
The particles will be heated in situ in a TEM across the premelting-to-melting regime.
Heating will begin at approximately 80% of the bulk melting temperature and continue upward.
Size- and shape-matched pure Ni nanoparticles will provide the baseline comparison.
Heating produces preferential segregation and clustering of one or more constituent elements at defect-rich surface regions.
Local compositional heterogeneities create regions with lower local melting points.
Lower-melting surface regions form initial liquid-like premelting zones.
Premelting fronts progressively invade the nanoparticle before the bulk melting transition.
FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will begin surface melting at a lower temperature than comparable pure Ni nanoparticles.
Premelting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will be accompanied by liquid-like surface layers and measurable compositional segregation.
Pure Ni nanoparticles will undergo a sharper and more spatially homogeneous melting transition near their bulk melting temperature.
Limited or moderate atomic mobility can retain a mixed five-element nanoparticle while allowing localized segregation.
The proposed behavior applies only when diffusion is sufficient for localized segregation to occur before melting.
Extensive atomic mobility may override segregation effects and invalidate the proposed mechanism.
A melting profile indistinguishable from that of size-matched Ni, or the absence of segregation-associated premelting fronts, would falsify the hypothesis.
